answer.summary: Laura Modi says “branding the mundane” means giving routine workflows and internal processes memorable names and stories. She says this can motivate people and improve memory recall, while making ordinary work feel more engaging.

sections.heading: What she means
sections.content: She means branding and storytelling ordinary workflows, frameworks, and parts of people’s jobs—not just external products. Her example is Airbnb’s “Air Dives”: a customer-service-ticket and pain-point analysis that people looked forward to hearing about on Fridays. She contrasts that name with the less compelling “customer service analysis.”

sections.heading: What it accomplishes
sections.content: Modi says this practice often keeps people motivated and improves memory recall. She also gives Bobbie’s “Secret Shopping Program” as an example: the legal and regulatory team checked content claims monthly and reported misleading or unclear claims for updates. Framing it as secret shopping made the activity more engaging than a routine report on claims mishaps.
